1: But to you, who find no fault, I will tell this most secret knowledge, together with its realization. Knowing it, you will be freed from what is inauspicious.
2: It is the king of knowledge and the king of secrets, the highest purifier. It is understood by direct perception, it accords with dharma, it is very easy to practise, and it is imperishable.
3: People who have no faith in this dharma, scorcher of foes, do not reach me. They turn back onto the path of death and the round of rebirth.
4: This whole world is pervaded by me, in my unmanifest form. All beings rest in me, and I do not rest in them.
5: And yet beings do not rest in me. See my lordly yoga. My self bears beings and does not rest in beings, and it brings beings into being.
6: As the great wind, which goes everywhere, always rests in space, so all beings rest in me. Understand it this way.
7: At the end of an aeon, son of Kuntī, all beings go into my own nature. At the beginning of an aeon I send them forth again.
8: Resting on my own nature, I send forth this whole multitude of beings again and again. The multitude is powerless: it comes forth by the power of nature.
9: And those actions do not bind me, winner of wealth. I sit like one who is indifferent, unattached to those actions.
10: With me as overseer, nature gives birth to all that moves and all that does not move. This is the cause, son of Kuntī, by which the world revolves.
11: The deluded despise me when I have taken a human body. They do not know my higher being as the great lord of beings.
12: Their hopes are vain, their actions are vain, their knowledge is vain, and they are without sense. They have taken to the deluding nature, the fiendish and indeed demonic one.
13: But those of great self, son of Pṛthā, take to the divine nature. Knowing me as the imperishable beginning of beings, they worship me with their minds on nothing else.
14: Constantly glorifying me, striving, firm in their vows, and bowing to me with devotion, they worship, always yoked.
15: And others too worship me by sacrificing with the sacrifice of knowledge. They worship me, who face in every direction, as one, as separate, in many ways.
16: I am the rite, I am the sacrifice, I am the offering to the ancestors, I am the healing herb. I am the sacred formula, I alone am the clarified butter, I am the fire, and I am what is offered.
17: I am the father of this world, its mother, its ordainer and its grandfather. I am what is to be known, the purifier, the syllable Oṁ, and the Ṛg Veda, the Sāma Veda and the Yajur Veda too.
18: I am the goal, the supporter, the lord, the witness, the dwelling, the refuge and the friend. I am the origin, the dissolution, the ground, the storehouse and the imperishable seed.
19: I give heat. I hold back the rain and I send it forth. I am both deathlessness and death, Arjuna, and both what is and what is not.
20: Those who know the three Vedas, who drink soma and are cleansed of evil, worship me with sacrifices and pray for the way to heaven. They reach the meritorious world of the lord of the gods, and there in heaven they feast on the heavenly enjoyments of the gods.
21: Having enjoyed that wide world of heaven, they enter the world of mortals when their merit is spent. So those who follow the dharma of the three Vedas, desiring pleasures, win going and coming.
22: The people who have no other, who think of me and worship me fully, are ever joined. For them I carry both the gaining and the keeping.
23: Even the devotees who worship other gods, filled with faith, are worshipping only me, son of Kuntī, though not according to rule.
24: For I am the enjoyer of all sacrifices, and indeed their lord. But they do not know me as I truly am, and so they fall.
25: Those vowed to the gods go to the gods. Those vowed to the ancestors go to the ancestors. Those who sacrifice to the spirits go to the spirits. And those who sacrifice to me, likewise, come to me.
26: When someone offers me a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water with devotion, I eat that offering, brought with devotion by one whose self is pure.
27: Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you pour in sacrifice, whatever you give, whatever austerity you practise, son of Kuntī, do it as an offering to me.
28: In this way you will be freed from the bonds of action, with their good and bad fruits. With the self joined to the yoga of renunciation, you will be set free and will come to me.
29: I am the same toward all beings. No one is hateful to me and no one is dear. But those who worship me with devotion are in me, and I too am in them.
30: Even if someone of very bad conduct worships me, devoted to no other, that person is to be thought of as good indeed, for that person has resolved rightly.
31: Such a person quickly becomes one whose self is dharma, and reaches everlasting peace. Son of Kuntī, declare it: my devotee does not perish.
32: For those who take refuge in me, son of Pṛthā, even if they are of evil birth, women, merchants and servants too, they also go to the highest goal.
33: How much more, then, the pure brahmins and the devoted royal seers. Having come to this impermanent, joyless world, worship me.
34: Keep your mind on me, be devoted to me, sacrifice to me, bow to me. Having joined the self in this way, with me as your highest goal, you will come to me alone.
